newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - June 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - June 20.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Times Of India
LALOO YADAV SEEKS ANTICIPATORY BAIL

Bihar state chief minister Laloo Prasad Yadav applied for anticipatory bail in the court of a special judge on Thursday. The court is likely to hear the bail plea on Friday. The petition argued that a political conspiracy was hatched against the petitioner, who is also the national president of the Janata Dal party. The election for the post of party president is to be held in a few weeks and the petitioner's arrest at this juncture is unwarranted and can influence the outcome of the election, the petition said.
The Hindustan Times
FOUR DEAD, 20 MISSING AS SHIP SINKS

Four people died and 20 are missing after merchant ship MMV Arcadia sank on Thursday off the coast of Bombay. Out of the 33 crew members aboard, nine were rescued. The four dead include the wife of the ship's captain. The captain and his four-year-old son are missing at sea. Ships and helicopters of the Indian Navy and the Coast Guard have joined the rescue operation.
The Economic Times
SHIP CARRYING TISCO CARGO SINKS IN HOOGHLY

A Korean liner named M.V. Green Opal flying a Panama flag and carrying about 6,000 tonnes of Tata Steel sank in the river Hooghly after colliding with a tug. The ship sank on Thursday, about 20 km (12 miles) away from the Calcutta port. All on board, including a crew of 20, were rescued by local fishermen. The tug named New Holland fled the scene after the collision but was later taken into custody and its crew arrested. It suffered little damage. The accident brought all ship movements to and from the Calcutta docks and the Budge Budge oil jetty to a complete halt. The accident was the first of its kind there in 30 years.
CHANGES IN RESERVE BANK ACT DUE, COMPANIES BILL IN JULY

Finance Minister P. Chidambaram said there would be more amendments to the Reserve Bank Act. He also said three major bills would be introduced in parliament next month and a fourth one in December. The bills revising the company law, foreign exchange management bill and the bill on money laundering will be introduced in July. The new income tax bill will be introduced in December. The minister expects the new insurance regulatory bill to become a law in July or August.
ROLE OF FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS' NOMINEES TO BE DISCUSSED

The finance secretary will discuss with the heads of financial institutions the specific role their nominees should play on the boards of companies. It is meant to improve corporate governance and the role the institutions can play in achieving it. There was a view that the institutional nominees should play a more active role in the boards of companies in the larger interests of corporate democracy. The view gained currency after cases of corruption and mismanagement surfaced in several big companies in which financial institutions had substantial stakes.
Financial Express
DAEWOO TO TAKE MARUTI ON

Daewoo Motors India is all set to challenge Indian auto makers like Maruti Udyog, General Motors India and Mahindra & Mahindra by launching five new vehicles within a year. The first one to roll out will be an 800-cc car. This car segment is now monopolised by the Maruti brand. The development of the car is in an advanced stage at the company's Pupyong plant. It is also developing 1,000-cc and 1,200-cc cars to take on the Zen and the Esteem from Maruti Udyog. Daewoo also plans to introduce in India its recently launched Nubira model.
FOREIGN INVESTMENT BOARD REJECTS NOKIA PROPOSAL

The Foreign Investment Promotion Board (FIPB) rejected telecommunications giant Nokia's proposal to use its wholly-owned investment subsidiary for trading. Subsidiary Nokia Telecommunication was set up as a holding company to promote ventures in India and hold equity stakes in them. Nokia applied the FIPB to allow the subsidiary to import and export telecommunications equipment and software too. But the FIPB rejected the application. Nokia wanted to take up trading activity through its holding company by importing and selling equipment in the Indian market and exporting products which it planned to manufacture there.
